Only rows 0-1 have a small grass patch at the corners. The ramp's sloped plane is not shown as a receding top surface. The ramp is drawn like a vertical wall panel between two thin vertical strips, dark brown on the left and orange on the right. These strips have constant width from row 2 to row 63, so they do not recede. Rows 64-79 are flat ground in front, with a dark line at row 63-64 marking the base. Nothing in the ramp reads as a 3/4-view top surface plus a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 8 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The ramp is built from about 5 tan-to-brown steps, with horizontal tread ridges and grain dots. The dark brown side walls and the green lip at the top are tinted material tones, not neutral black. The 0% near-neutral share of dark edge pixels confirms the tint, unlike the paving reference at 80%. The lower landing is a little flatter and sparser than the ramp, and the ridges are fairly regular. Overall it holds up beside the references without looking thinner or more sticker-like.
